definitions.gloss: difficult to read; hard to decipher
definitions.explanation: Describes text, kanji, or names that are difficult to read correctly. Most commonly used in the compound 難読漢字 (hard-to-read kanji) referring to kanji with unusual or rare readings.

examples.japanese: ⟦これ→これ：00963_kore⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{難読|なんどく}{漢字|かんじ}だ。
⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{難読|なんどく}⟦{地名|ちめい}→地名：04059_chimei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There are many hard-to-read place names in Japan.

examples.japanese: {難読|なんどく}{名字|みょうじ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}→持ち主：10439_mochinushi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{読|よ}み{方|かた}→読み方：14269_yomikata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{説明|せつめい}→説明：01449_setsumei⟧し⟦なければならない→なければならない：27600_nakerebanaranai⟧。
examples.english: People with hard-to-read surnames always have to explain how to read their names.

notes:
COMPOUNDS:
- {難読|なんどく}{漢字|かんじ} (hard-to-read kanji)
- {難読|なんどく}⟦{地名|ちめい}→地名：04059_chimei⟧ (hard-to-read place names)
- {難読|なんどく}{名字|みょうじ} (hard-to-read surnames)
- {難読|なんどく}⟦{語|ご}→〜語：09841_go⟧ (hard-to-read words)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Kanji quizzes featuring {難読|なんどく}{漢字|かんじ} are a popular form of entertainment in Japan, appearing in TV quiz shows, books, and online content. Common examples include ⟦{薔薇|ばら}→薔薇：04390_bara⟧ (rose), ⟦{蝸牛|かたつむり}→蝸牛：04297_katatsumuri⟧ (snail), and ⟦{海豚|いるか}→海豚：04313_iruka⟧ (dolphin).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{読|よ}み→読む：00426_yomu⟧にくい: Hard to read — more general, can refer to handwriting, small print, or poor formatting, not just kanji difficulty.
